title: R. W. Saaty college selection example - two matrices with published CRs
description: The college-selection walkthrough from R. W. Saaty's 1987 overview paper: a candidate compares five colleges on four criteria. The paper prints two of the matrices in full, each with its priority vector and, unusually for the literature, its consistency ratio: the criteria matrix (weights 0.053, 0.491, 0.238, 0.213 as printed, 'inconsistency ratio of 0.02') and the LOCATION matrix for the five colleges (weights 0.115, 0.402, 0.283, 0.163, 0.037, 'C.R. = 0.092'). Both published CRs recompute from the printed matrices at the published precision and are the normative expected CR values here, making this the fixture of record for a known-CR inconsistent matrix from the literature (the drinks fixture's CR 0.022 is the other). Expected priorities are derived at six decimals because the paper publishes at three with documented rounding quirks - see source_reported. The paper notes the calculations were made with the Expert Choice software; the remaining three college matrices are not printed (only their priority vectors), so they are not included.

source.citation: R. W. Saaty, 'The analytic hierarchy process - what it is and how it is used', Mathematical Modelling 9(3-5), 1987, pp. 161-176; college selection example, pp. 163-166 (criteria matrix and weights p. 164, LOCATION matrix with weights and C.R. p. 165, synthesis p. 166).

provenance.method: Principal right eigenvector of the pairwise comparison matrix (computed with numpy.linalg.eig; the Perron root is lambda_max), normalized to sum to 1. CI = (lambda_max - n)/(n - 1); CR = CI / RI(n) for the RI table declared in this fixture. Reproduce with tools/compute_expected.py.

source_reported.explanation: The paper prints the criteria weights as (0.053, 0.491, 0.238, 0.213). Recomputation from the printed matrix gives (0.0528, 0.4910, 0.2382, 0.2180): the first three agree at the printed precision, while ACADEMICS recomputes as 0.218 rather than 0.213. Three observations indicate a typographical slip in the last digit: the printed vector sums to 0.995 while the recomputed one sums to 1.000; and re-synthesizing with 0.218 and the paper's published local vectors reproduces the paper's published final priorities (0.270, 0.387, 0.201, 0.086, 0.055) within 0.001 of every printed value, while 0.213 leaves the top two 0.003 short. For the LOCATION matrix, the printed weight for U. Michigan is 0.283 where the exact value is 0.2841, consistent with rounding the vector to sum to 1.000. The paper's published local priority vectors for the three matrices it does not print (Ambience, Reputation, Academics) and its final synthesis are preserved here as context; they are not expected values because their matrices are not published.
